local_articles.title: Spieth among 5 sharing lead as PGA play-offs open
local_articles.snippet: WASHINGTON – Three-time Major winner Jordan Spieth, trying to end a four-year victory drought, fired a seven-under 65 to share the lead after the first round of the PGA Tour St Jude Championship on Aug 13. Fellow Americans Jake Knapp, Kurt Kitayama, Michael Thorbjornsen and Michael Kim were also at 65 after 18 holes in the FedEx Cup play-off opener under sweltering conditions at TPC Southwind in Memphis, Tennessee. It marked the most players to share the lead in any play-off event after the first round. Hot on their heels on 66 was a pack including Major winners Adam Scott, Gary Woodland and Hideki Matsuyama plus defending play-off champion Tommy Fleetwood. “Heat is the biggest challenge,” said Scott, 46. “Just pacing yourself. local_articles.title: Rory McIlroy suffers from rustiness in opening-round 74 at St Jude Championship
local_articles.snippet: Rory McIlroy’s lack of sharpness was exposed as he struggled in the first round of the St Jude Championship at TPC Southwind in Memphis. The Northern Irishman – playing for the first time since last month’s Open – opened with a four-over-par 74. This tournament is the first of three to close out the FedEx Cup playoffs on the PGA Tour. Jordan Spieth – without a top-10 all season on tour – rediscovered his form to join recent Rocket Classic winner Michael Thorbjornsen and Kurt Kitayama in a share of the clubhouse lead on five-under-par 65,. For McIlroy, though, the return to tournament action proved hugely disappointing. The world No 2 finished six-five-six – bogey, bogey, double bogey – in a poor conclusion to his round. questions.current_reasoning: Recalibrating the Aug 16 Cardiff FA Community Shield from stale July 23 54/46 to market-consensus 51/49 based on Aug 9-11 multi-book odds and squad/preseason updates (The Fair Stake/Ladbrokes, Record.pt/Betclic/Solverde/Lebull, talkSPORT Aug 10; Sports Mole Aug 9; Betway, Hindustan Times, local Khaleej Times/Straits Times/Al Jazeera Aug 9-11): Four sportsbooks converge almost identically on a coin-flip trophy market—Ladbrokes 90-min odds 6/4 Arsenal, 5/2 Draw, 13/8 Man City de-vig to 50.9% Arsenal / 49.1% City (assuming 50/50 straight-to-penalties shootout, where 6 of the last 10 Community Shields were decided; 50.4%/49.6% with slight Donnarumma shootout edge), with Lebull (50.8%), Betclic (51.3%), and Solverde (50.0%) averaging 50.7% Arsenal. Team news explains the narrowing: although Arsenal completed the GBP 75m signing of Bruno Guimaraes (Aug 8) and welcome David Raya/Bukayo Saka back to training ahead of Wednesday's Como friendly, Arteta confirmed Aug 9 that BOTH William Saliba (back, 2-week complete rest) and Jurrien Timber (groin, 'still weeks away') are OUT, and Arsenal conceded 6 goals in back-to-back friendly losses (3-1 Betis Aug 5, 3-2 Borussia Dortmund Aug 9). Meanwhile, despite Rodri missing out (back surgery) and Haaland/Anderson/Guehi/O'Reilly/Doku returning to training only Wednesday Aug 12, Enzo Maresca's City finished their Asia tour sharply with a 3-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Seoul (Aug 9, Omar Marmoush brace, Antoine Semenyo 2 assists).
